prompt:
Act as an expert full-stack developer and create a production-ready, beautiful digital storefront platform clone of Podia using Next.js 15 (App Router), TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Stripe, and PostgreSQL (via Drizzle ORM). The application must feature a breathtaking, modern user interface utilizing glassmorphism, smooth micro-animations (using Framer Motion), and a meticulously crafted design system using rich, harmonious colors and premium typography (like Inter or Outfit). The UI must feel incredibly premium, responsive, and alive.

Core Features & Functionality:
1. Beautiful Storefront: A stunning, highly optimized public-facing `/store` index showcasing a list of digital products. Each product should have a dedicated page featuring high-quality images, rich descriptions, and a frictionless 'Buy' button routing to Stripe Checkout.
2. Secure Digital Delivery: After successful Stripe payment, securely generate and email a signed, short-lived download link (e.g., expiring in 7 days or 5 uses) to the buyer using Resend or SMTP. If a link expires, provide an elegant flow to request a new one.
3. Product Management: An admin dashboard for the creator to manage digital products (title, price, description, file upload). Store digital files securely in S3-compatible storage, outside the public web root.
4. Order Tracking & CRM: A comprehensive admin view to monitor orders, revenue per product, and customer details. 
5. Security & Robustness: Verify every Stripe webhook signature to ensure orders are securely recorded in PostgreSQL. Add strict input validation and graceful error handling.

Technical Architecture & Best Practices:
- Frontend: Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS. Use shadcn/ui for accessible, highly polished foundation components.
- Backend & DB: Next.js Route Handlers. PostgreSQL with Drizzle ORM.
- Payments: Stripe Checkout integration with robust webhook handling.
- SEO & Performance: Implement automatic meta tags, semantic HTML5, localized loading states, and flawless error boundaries.

Implementation Requirements:
Start from an empty repository and build the complete working project. Store all user data locally by default and ensure straightforward data export. Put all secrets in `.env` and ship a `.env.example`. Make the first run work locally with one documented command.

Deliverables:
Provide the full, deployable codebase. Include a detailed `README.md` covering setup, architecture, Stripe webhook configuration, and local testing instructions. Write focused unit tests for the core data model. Deliberately exclude: complex memberships, drip courses, email marketing automation, and affiliate networks. Focus relentlessly on delivering a flawless, visually spectacular digital download sales experience.
